about: One opportunity per institution. Closed won = every artifact identified and accounted for: every known artifact and evidence item for that body identified, located and viewed in the catalogue. Each pipeline is the worst case: the body denies, admits nothing and takes the longest lawful time at every stage.

data_state.note: The river flow (data/flows.json, 0.0.2) carries the correspondence of the last 18 months per institution: requests, internal reviews, complaints, regulator cases, outcomes and the artifacts received. The stage pipelines below are still the worst-case framework: markers sit at the start and no stage carries a light until stage-level import.

forecast_rules.lawful_maximum: Every stage takes its clock plus the longest extension the law or policy allows.
forecast_rules.lateness: A body that misses its deadline does not lengthen the forecast: the day after the lawful maximum is the day we escalate.
forecast_rules.laps: Laps run one after another; inside a lap, stages that depend on each other run in order and the rest run side by side.
forecast_rules.clarification: Worst case: the body asks for clarification on the last day and the clock starts again from our answer.
forecast_rules.working_days: Working days skip weekends and any UK bank holiday (FOIA s.10(6), EIR reg 2). Bank holidays are published to 2028-12-26; later dates count weekends only.
forecast_rules.unpublished_times: Where no time is published, the seeded ladder's assumption is used and the stage is marked inferred.

clock_units.wd: working days (UK bank holidays in any part of the UK excluded: FOIA s.10(6), EIR reg 2)

lights.label: Red
lights.meaning: Concluded with a refusal, not held, no reply, or an excuse: escalate.

lights.label: Amber
lights.meaning: Concluded with a late, partial or doubtful answer: escalate.

no_green: There is no green: no answer is taken as satisfactory, which is why every stage escalates to the next.

excuses.label: Away on holiday / staff absent
excuses.law: FOIA 2000 s.10(6): only weekends and UK bank holidays stop the 20 working days; leave does not
excuses.counter: Note the due date; at the lawful maximum, escalate.

excuses.label: Paywall / fee demanded
excuses.law: FOIA s.9 fees notice and s.13; EIR reg 8 (reasonable charge); UK GDPR Art 12(5): a SAR is free unless manifestly unfounded or excessive
excuses.counter: Ask for the fee basis in writing; the clock pauses only for a valid fees notice.

excuses.label: That old chestnut (stock excuse)
excuses.law: Any stock form of words offered instead of a search; each one is catalogued at /that-old-chestnut/
excuses.counter: Quote the words back and ask for the search made.

excuses.label: Fire, flood or other loss
excuses.law: Code of Practice on the management of records (FOIA s.46): records kept, disposed of and logged
excuses.counter: Ask for the incident record and the disposal or loss log.

excuses.label: Records destroyed or presumed destroyed
excuses.law: FOIA s.77 and EIR reg 19: destroying or concealing records after a request is an offence; s.46 Code: disposal must be logged
excuses.counter: Ask for the destruction schedule entry, its date and authority.

excuses.label: Not held
excuses.law: FOIA s.1(1)(a); EIR reg 12(4)(a): the body must say whether it holds the information, after an adequate search
excuses.counter: Ask where and how it searched (ICO: the search must be reasonable).

excuses.label: Cost limit / too much work
excuses.law: FOIA s.12 appropriate limit (£600 central government, £450 others, Fees Regulations 2004); EIR reg 12(4)(b) burden limb
excuses.counter: Ask for the estimate and for advice to narrow (s.16).

excuses.label: Vexatious or repeated
excuses.law: FOIA s.14(1) vexatious, s.14(2) repeated; EIR reg 12(4)(b) manifestly unreasonable
excuses.counter: Internal review, then ICO: the burden is on the body to show it.

excuses.label: Publicly available elsewhere
excuses.law: FOIA s.21; EIR reg 6(1)(b): only for information the body itself holds and that is reasonably accessible
excuses.counter: Ask for the exact location of the item said to be available.

excuses.label: Scope narrowed / request re-read
excuses.law: FOIA s.16 duty to advise; s.45 Code of Practice: requests read objectively
excuses.counter: Restate the request in full with every name the place is known by.

excuses.label: Clarification demanded (clock reset)
excuses.law: FOIA s.1(3); EIR reg 9(2)-(4): the clock runs again from our answer
excuses.counter: Answer the same day; log the restart date.

excuses.label: Sent elsewhere (not our remit)
excuses.law: EIR reg 10 transfer; FOIA s.45 Code of Practice: advise or transfer, do not just signpost
excuses.counter: Ask whether it holds anything at all, then open the named body's pipeline.

excuses.label: Not subject to FOI
excuses.law: FOIA s.3 and Sch 1; EIR reg 2(2)(c)-(d): bodies with public administrative functions are covered by the EIR
excuses.counter: Use the EIR test, a SAR or the body's own policy instead.

excuses.label: Withheld as personal data ("GDPR")
excuses.law: FOIA s.40(2); EIR reg 13; DPA 2018 s.3(2): personal data means data about a living person
excuses.counter: Ask which living person; records of the dead are not personal data.

excuses.label: Lost in post / mailbox not watched
excuses.law: FOIA s.8: a request by email is a valid written request; the clock runs from receipt
excuses.counter: Keep the delivery record; resend to a second published address.

excuses.label: Volume of work (delay)
excuses.law: FOIA s.10(1) / EIR reg 5(2): 20 working days whatever the workload
excuses.counter: Note the due date; at the lawful maximum, escalate.

excuses.label: No reply by the due date (the dartboard's red house)
excuses.law: FOIA s.10(1); UK GDPR Art 12(3): the time limit is the limit
excuses.counter: Escalate the day after the lawful maximum.

excuses.label: Late or part answer (the dartboard's red fish)
excuses.law: FOIA s.1(1), s.10(1), s.17 refusal notice for anything withheld
excuses.counter: Ask for the refusal notice for the part not answered.

changelog.change: Emails come from the central catalogue: every build pulls the email metadata (id, date, direction, correspondent, subject line, thread, request record) into data/catalogue-emails.json and links each email to its catalogue record (EV-0906 onwards, the EV series). The ERP keeps no email text. Additive: erp.json schema unchanged.

River flow 0.2.0 and data/flows.json: the correspondence of the last 18 months imported from the case-mail index, cross-checked against Gmail, the evidence catalogue and the dartboard; one line per enquiry type with internal review, complaint and regulator splits; outcome icons; presents for artifacts received as attachments, each opening its catalogue entry. Goal renamed: every artifact identified and accounted for. Additive: erp.json schema unchanged.
First release: schema 1.0.0, 56 worst-case pipelines seeded from the forecast ladders and the That Old Chestnut excuses; takes slot 57 of 59.
